claims.text: Laser-assisted machining with laser preheating and a TiAlN/SH-coated end mill will improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy.
The intervention will reduce machining-induced surface defects and residual stresses.
Laser preheating increases local ductility during machining.
Increased local ductility minimizes crack formation and propagation during machining.
A TiAlN/SH-coated end mill sustains cutting performance at elevated temperatures.
Sustained cutting performance from the coated end mill improves the machined surface finish.
Reducing micro-cracks, residual stresses, and surface defects produces a refined near-surface microstructure.
The proposed processing enhances grain-boundary cohesion near the surface.
The improved near-surface microstructure better supports elevated-temperature mechanical performance.
Laser-assisted machined samples will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than conventionally machined samples.
Laser-assisted machined samples will have better elevated-temperature creep resistance than conventionally machined samples.
Conventional machining with standard end mills typically produces higher surface-defect densities in this alloy than the proposed intervention.
Conventional machining with standard end mills typically produces higher residual stresses in this alloy than the proposed intervention.
The intervention is expected to remain effective when laser preheating is kept below temperatures that cause melting or unwanted phase transformations.
The target alloy contains at least five elements, with titanium and nickel as primary constituents and constituent concentrations within the stated 5–35 at% high-entropy range.
